methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Commentary explicitly diagnosing how AI data center infrastructure concentrates economic benefits in urban corridors while rural areas bear environmental costs without capability-building, signaling structural barriers to distributed AI adoption.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU-AI Ready RVA partnership creates institutional infrastructure for broad-based AI education and community engagement in Richmond, potentially seeding peer-to-peer capability development beyond elite tech hubs if implementation follows through.

signals.title: EPA grant backs community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: EPA-funded community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia represents grassroots capacity-building in historically underserved coal transition region, testing whether distributed deep learning can emerge from place-based economic development rather than metro overflow.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Platform AI tools creating workforce pressure on Richmond's young workers signals rapid shallow adoption through consumer/enterprise software rather than deep technical capability development, potentially widening skill gaps even as usage spreads.

signals.title: Why Darden Is Moving AI Into the Core MBA Experience - Darden Report Online
signals.signal_reading: Darden MBA integrating AI into core curriculum deepens elite institutional capability in Charlottesville but concentration in premium business education limits accessibility, reinforcing credential-based stratification in AI fluency across Virginia's workforce.
